correctness.rationale: Exact majority-margin coupling yields equation (1) and the stationary trinomial balance identity. Fourier inversion of the positive symbol L gives a probability-tilt identity in which the neighboring return-probability ratio has strictly positive increments equal to a scaled variance. Its limit is sqrt(a/b); exact squares give the sign p+q-1. Strong law, zero-drift CLT, and parameter continuity settle boundaries and arbitrary crossover delay. An independently implemented rational binomial and convolution verifier passes 840 assertions. No finite check is treated as an infinite proof.

originality.rationale: Semantic overlap queries and comparisons with previously available mathematical claims were compared to the exact statement. The closest full text with a monotonicity theorem assumes all voters competent and randomized subcommittee selection (Berend–Sapir 2005), whereas this model appends one below-chance voter at every pair and classifies all odd sizes via a novel monotone trinomial return-probability ratio. The 2016 exact majority formula does not settle the claim; an explicit parameter choice violates its broad unqualified finite monotonicity assertion. A 2026 full-source examination concerns exchangeable repetition and is inapplicable. The missing full 2007 dependent-jury article is an explicit residual priority risk. Historical novelty is provisional rather than absolute.
residual_risks: An equivalent deterministic two-type monotonicity theorem might occur in earlier, differently indexed social-choice or Poisson-binomial research.
Complete text of Berend–Sapir 2007 dependent-jury extension was unavailable; only its random-subcommittee abstract could be compared.

value.rationale: A natural alternating recruitment policy permits below-chance independent voters, and its committee-size accuracy exhibits an exact sharp dichotomy: perpetual decay or a unique trough followed by asymptotic recovery, with the first expansion always harmful. It supplies all-size qualitative control and a testable counterexample to naive inference from average competence; the crossover may be arbitrarily delayed. The specific nested protocol is structurally motivated, not an arbitrary isolated parameter slice, and the analytic statement is more than the computational example.
